findings.title: `queued` default evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a class-level default evaluated when the module is first imported, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit `queued` shares the process start time instead of the actual creation time. This makes the field useless for diagnosing/ordering sync events (and misleading in logs). Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

findings.title: Non-JSON-serializable datetime passed in Celery task kwargs
findings.body: `assignment_source.to_dict()` (via `dataclasses.asdict`) includes the `queued` datetime object, which is placed into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs=...)`. With a JSON task serializer this raises a serialization error and the outbound assignee sync task is never queued, silently breaking all outbound assignee syncs whenever an assignment_source is present. Serialize `queued` to an ISO string (and parse it back in `from_dict`).

findings.title: from_dict does not validate/convert field types
findings.body: `from_dict` simply splats the dict into the constructor, so a round-tripped `queued` string stays a `str` and `integration_id` could be any type (e.g. a string from JSON), with no error. Downstream comparisons like `sync_source.integration_id == org_integration.integration_id` would then fail silently (string vs int), defeating the cycle-breaking logic. Coerce/validate types explicitly.

findings.title: New `assignment_source` kwarg may break existing sync_assignee_outbound implementations
findings.body: The task now always passes `assignment_source=...` to `installation.sync_assignee_outbound`. Concrete implementations (Jira, Jira Server, VSTS, GitHub Enterprise, etc.) whose signatures are `(self, external_issue, user, assign=True, **kwargs)` are fine, but any implementation without `**kwargs` will raise TypeError at runtime. The abstract signature in `mixins/issues.py` was not updated to include `assignment_source` either, so implementers get no signal. Add the parameter to the abstract signature and verify every override accepts it.
